text: Risk management is an important process in both business and daily life. It begins with identifying potential risks that could cause problems, such as financial losses or project delays. Once these risks are identified, you need to develop mitigation strategies to reduce their impact. For example, you might improve safety procedures or diversify your investments. It is also essential to have contingency plans in place. These are backup actions you will take if a risk actually occurs, like having emergency funds or alternative suppliers. Finally, you should continuously monitor the situation, as risks can change over time. By following these steps, you can handle uncertainties more effectively and make better decisions.
